title: Panel Review Findings
description: Structured output contract every reviewer sub-agent conforms to

reviewer.description: The persona that produced this output (e.g. 'correctness', 'security')

findings.description: The reviewer's findings. Empty array when nothing was found.

title.description: A short, specific issue title — 10 words or fewer.

line.description: Primary line number of the issue

why_it_matters.description: The impact and failure mode — not 'what is wrong' but 'what breaks'

autofix_class.description: Routing signal for the caller after review (the skill itself applies in interactive mode by judgment, not from this field). gated_auto = a concrete suggested_fix is proposed; the caller applies after judgment. manual = needs design input or a cross-cutting decision. advisory = report-only.

owner.description: Who should own the next action for this finding after synthesis

requires_verification.description: Whether any fix for this finding must be re-verified with targeted tests or a follow-up review pass

suggested_fix.description: A concrete, minimal fix the reviewer can defend from the diff and surrounding code. Propose one whenever any defensible change is reachable from review context (a parallel pattern in the repo, a framework convention, or the cited code itself). Imperfect information is not a reason to omit — propose the most defensible default for what you can see, name the assumption you are making, and let the user override. 'I need <X> before I can commit' is a soft punt: the real question is 'what change would I propose if I had to choose now?' — propose that, with the assumption named. Omit only when there is genuinely no code-level change to propose — the finding is a question rather than a fix ('what SLA is intended here?'), or the resolution is purely organizational (a policy or sign-off with no code component). Those cases are rare in code review. A bad suggestion is worse than none, but a soft punt is the failure this field exists to prevent.

confidence.description: Anchored confidence. Use exactly one of 0, 25, 50, 75, 100 — each anchor carries a behavioral criterion the reviewer must honestly self-apply. 0: Not confident — a false positive that does not survive light scrutiny, or a pre-existing issue this change did not introduce. 25: Somewhat confident — might be real, might be a false positive; could not be verified from the diff and surrounding code alone. 50: Moderately confident — verified real but a nitpick, a narrow edge case, or low practical impact; style preferences and subjective improvements land here. 75: Highly confident — double-checked and confirmed the issue affects users, callers, or runtime in normal usage; the bug, vulnerability, or contract violation is clearly present and actionable. 100: Certain — verifiable from the code itself (compile/type error, definitive logic bug, or a quotable standards violation); no interpretation required.

evidence.description: Code-grounded evidence — snippets, line references, or pattern descriptions. At least one item.

pre_existing.description: True when the issue lives in unchanged code unrelated to this diff

residual_risks.description: Risks the reviewer noticed but could not confirm as findings

testing_gaps.description: Missing test coverage the reviewer identified

confidence_anchors.description: Confidence is one of 5 discrete anchors (0, 25, 50, 75, 100), each tied to a behavioral criterion the reviewer can honestly self-apply. Float values (e.g. 0.73) are invalid — the model cannot meaningfully calibrate at finer granularity, and discrete anchors prevent false-precision gaming.
confidence_anchors.0: False positive or pre-existing — do not report
confidence_anchors.25: Speculative; could not verify — do not report
confidence_anchors.50: Verified real but minor or stylistic — report only when P0, or when synthesis routes to advisory / soft buckets
confidence_anchors.75: Highly confident; affects users or runtime in normal usage — report
confidence_anchors.100: Verifiable from code alone (compile/type error, definitive logic bug, quoted standards violation) — report

confidence_thresholds.suppress: Below anchor 75 — do not report. Exception: P0 findings at anchor 50+ may be reported (a critical-but-uncertain issue must not be dropped silently).
confidence_thresholds.report: Anchor 75 or 100 — include with full evidence.

severity_definitions.P0: Critical breakage, exploitable vulnerability, data loss/corruption. Must fix before merge.
severity_definitions.P1: High-impact defect hit in normal usage, or a broken contract. Should fix.
severity_definitions.P2: Moderate downside (edge case, perf regression, maintainability trap). Fix if straightforward.
severity_definitions.P3: Low impact, narrow scope, minor improvement. Reviewer's discretion.

autofix_classes.gated_auto: A concrete suggested_fix is proposed. The caller may apply after judgment — not this skill mechanically.
autofix_classes.manual: Actionable, but needs a design decision or a cross-cutting change.
autofix_classes.advisory: Informational or operational item for the report only.

owners.downstream-resolver: The caller or a human should act after the review.

return_tiers.description: Finding fields split into two tiers. The full schema (all required fields) applies to the artifact file on disk. The compact return to the orchestrator omits the detail tier. Both are valid uses of this schema in different contexts.
return_tiers.merge_tier: Returned to the orchestrator: title, severity, file, line, confidence, autofix_class, owner, requires_verification, pre_existing, suggested_fix (optional). Plus top-level reviewer, residual_risks, testing_gaps.
return_tiers.detail_tier: Required in the artifact file, omitted from the compact return: why_it_matters, evidence. The artifact file must pass full schema validation including all required fields. Agent-mode (JSON) output depends on why_it_matters and evidence being present in the artifact.
